definition: A manifest variable is a directly observed measure used in an analysis, in contrast to a latent variable that reflects differences across individuals that are not directly observed. In this source, the within-person relationship between planning time and execution time is described as occurring at the manifest-variable level after accounting for across-person relationships.

reasons: The packet does not define a manifest variable as a “directly observed measure”; it only contrasts relationships “across individuals (at the latent variable level)” with relationships “within individuals (at the manifest variable level).

The definition’s claim that manifest variables “reflect differences across individuals that are not directly observed” is reversed relative to the packet’s description (the packet attributes across-individual differences to the latent-variable level, not to manifest variables).

The specific phrasing about the “within-person relationship between planning time and execution time … at the manifest-variable level after accounting for across-person relationships” is supported only at a high level (within- vs across-individual relationship), but the broader measurement/observation claims are not supported.

The packet supports a within-individual, manifest-variable level relationship after controlling for across-individual relationships, but it does not explicitly define a manifest variable as a directly observed measure or define latent variables as unobserved differences across individuals.
The first sentence generalizes beyond the source text by giving a broader methodological definition that is not stated in the packet.
